```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Demand evidence is broader in A. It cites three separately sourced Reddit posts (structural engineer, HR practitioner, therapist) describing multi-state licensing pain. B has only one sourced quote, because its second quote's URL was 'not retrieved' and so counts as missing.",
    "A's MVP is a deadline database with alerts and documents, scoped as 'tracking only, not legal advice.' That posture is already used by live comparables (ExpirationOps, NeverFined), which suggests a thin version can reach paying customers quickly. B's MVP must produce AI price estimates accurate enough that contractors will send them unedited. B's own brief flags that accuracy and trust bar as a risk that a fast MVP may not clear.",
    "A's acquisition data fits the category better. It cites sourced category CPCs ($10-13) and observes that competitors converge on long-tail SEO. B's acquisition evidence is weaker: a generic B2B SaaS blended CPL of $237 and a Google CPC range of '$0.01 to $10+'. Neither is specific enough to plan a 90-day channel for time-poor, software-skeptical contractors.",
    "B's case for relies on an unsourced claim that several competitors are run by single contractor-founders. It also bundles 'schedules crews', which its own brief calls integration-heavy and unlikely to work within six weeks. Both points add scope risk to a 90-day paid-customer goal.",
    "Both markets are equally crowded, with seven live competitors each, so crowding does not separate them. A's competitors publish clear low-end price points ($29-99/mo, $49/mo). That anchors a price hypothesis for a solo entrant at least as well as B's anchors do."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's demand evidence. Only one quote is sourced (the r/estimators post about 1-2 hours of nightly quoting). The second quote ('half your week driving around...') is flagged in B's unsourced claims as having an unretrieved URL, so it counts as missing. B's case for also rests on the unsourced assertion that competitors like EstimationPro and Outdoor Estimates are run by single contractor-founders.",
  "confidence_note": "Low-to-moderate confidence. Both briefs describe crowded markets with seven competitors and no clear wedge. A has its own serious weaknesses. Its three demand quotes come from individual professional licensees (engineer, therapist, HR), not the stated payer of finance/ops leads at multi-state firms. Its own case against argues that a six-week build yields a static tracker that is a strict subset of $29-49/mo incumbents. A wins mainly on more sourced demand evidence and a lower-stakes MVP, not on a demonstrated path to a first paying customer."
}
```
